scenarios.desc: Push recipe proposes a second lock path in /tmp
scenarios.input: I am adding a push recipe to a runbook. To serialize pushes I plan to use `flock /tmp/aiagents-push.lock git push origin "$BR"`. Plan in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: flock excludes only processes opening the same path, so a second path is a second scheme that excludes nothing. The rule mandates $HOME/src/scratch/locks/push-lock-<slug>.lock and forbids /tmp, which was wiped mid-session and split the lock across two inodes under one filename.

scenarios.desc: Lock keyed on something other than the branch
scenarios.input: To cut contention I want to hash the branch name into four lock slots so pushes share a small pool of lock files. Plan in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: git takes its own lock per ref, so unrelated branches serializing behind a 10 to 16 minute pre-push hook is pure waste. The measured hashed four-slot scheme collided two different branches about 25 percent of the time.

scenarios.desc: Recording a historical census of the old schemes
scenarios.input: I am writing a retrospective that quotes the old `flock /tmp/aiagents-push.lock` command as evidence of what the previous scheme looked like. Plan in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: A census or retrospective records what the old schemes looked like and is evidence, not a prescription. The rule exempts such a fenced block when it carries the push-lock-historical token, and the checker already skips the retrospective, audit, and archive trees.

scenarios.desc: Adding an unrelated shell command to a runbook (negative)
scenarios.input: I want to document `git log --oneline -5` in a runbook so contributors can check recent commits. Plan in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: The command opens no lock and serializes nothing, so the push-lock discipline does not apply.
